hypothesis: A handwriting sample may be verified more robustly across scripts by its ordered relation pattern to fit writers than by directly comparing its absolute embedding coordinates.
reference_definition: Each fit writer contributes one Arabic prototype and one English prototype in the same fixed writer order.
verification_definition: Arabic samples are represented by cosine relations to Arabic fit-writer prototypes; English samples use the corresponding English prototypes; fingerprints are L2-normalized and compared with cosine similarity.
useful_auc_gain: relation fingerprint minus raw cross-script macro AUC >= 0.01
strong_auc_gain: relation fingerprint minus raw cross-script macro AUC >= 0.03
useful_eer_reduction: pooled EER decreases by at least 0.01 absolute

interpretation_cases.strong_support: At least one encoder gains >= 0.03 macro AUC and its pooled EER does not increase by more than 0.005 absolute.
interpretation_cases.promising_support: At least one encoder gains >= 0.01 but less than 0.03 macro AUC.
interpretation_cases.no_meaningful_support: Both encoders gain less than 0.01 macro AUC.
interpretation_cases.harmful: Relation fingerprints decrease macro AUC for both encoders.

wgc_coupling_interpretation.wgc_benefits_more: The WGC-trained geometry is especially useful when verification directly reads relational structure.
wgc_coupling_interpretation.both_benefit_similarly: Relation fingerprints may be a useful general backend rather than specifically a WGC mechanism.
wgc_coupling_interpretation.wgc_advantage_disappears: The relational backend may explain or replace part of the previous WGC advantage.
